walkthroughs.body_html:
Solar System -> Milky Way galaxy -> Universe.

Distances measured in light years.

Low mass: protostar -> main sequence -> red giant -> white dwarf.

High mass: -> red supergiant -> supernova -> neutron star or black hole.

Distant galaxies are moving away.

Light stretched -> longer wavelength.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between nuclear fission and fusion?
options: It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
Fission splits a heavy nucleus into smaller ones; fusion joins light nuclei into a heavier one.
Fission and fusion are the same process, just at different scales.
Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.

mcqs.q: Why is nuclear fusion much harder to achieve on Earth than fission?
options: Fusion is harder because the materials are rarer than uranium.
Fusion is harder because you need to break atoms apart first.
Fusion requires extremely high temperatures and pressures to overcome the electrostatic repulsion between positive nuclei.
Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.

mcqs.q: If one EM wave has a higher frequency than another, what is true about its wavelength?
options: It is also longer, because both increase together.
It is shorter — wavelength and frequency are inversely related (c = f x lambda).
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.
